extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of poetry, drama, and literary composition (poets, dramatists, literary theorists)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts guidance from Aristotle's Poetics on composing imitative art (epic, tragedy, comedy, dithyramb), including genre choices, modes/mechanisms of imitation, and appropriate use/mixing of meter, diction, and music. Useful for writers structuring narrative/verse and choosing expressive means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre classification and subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Epopoeia (epic) which sings of heroes; tragedy sings of the unhappy falls of princes; comedy uses the ridiculous; dithyrambic poetry sings Bacchus; and other kinds (aulèticae, citharisticae, etc.) – all are imitations but differ in subject and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the genre whose subject-matter and affect suit your material: use epic for heroic narrative, tragedy for princely tragedy/unhappy reversals, comedy when the ridiculous is central, dithyramb for Bacchic/ecstatic themes; other species have their own typical subjects and tones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threefold distinction of imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitations differ three ways: (1) by the instruments or means of imitation (quibus instrumentis), (2) by the objects or things imitated (diversas res), and (3) by the manner or mode of imitation (diverso, et non eodem imitandi modo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing, decide along which axis you will shape the work: select the medium (speech, meter, music), the subject-matter to be represented, and the manner (narrative, enacted, lyrical) appropriate to the intended effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruments/means of imitation (number, diction, harmony)
rubrics_metrics.description: The arts use instruments such as NUMERO (metrical/rhythmic motion), ORATIONE (speech/diction), and HARMONIA (melody/harmony of the voice); these can be taken singly or combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhythm (meter), spoken diction, and musical/harmonic elements consciously: select one or combine them to suit genre and effect (e.g., lyric with melody and meter, narrative with meter and diction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing and tempering of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The instruments (number, oration, harmony) may be taken severally, or mixed together, or combined and tempered with one another (aut segillatim seorsimque sumptis, aut inter se mixtis, simulque temperatis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend metrical, vocal, and musical resources as needed; temper the balance so no single element overwhelms the intended imitation. Examples in the text: aulos and citharistic arts mix number and harmony differently; some arts (flute/dancers) may use number without harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic (epopoeia) uses meter (number) without harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: Epopoeia imitates by number, not by harmony, but by naked speeches in meters (Epopoeia veto, arc numero imitatur, nec harmonia, sed solum sermonibus nudis, sive appellare malumus, metris).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing epic/narrative poetry, rely primarily on metrical structures and versified speech rather than melodic/harmonic musical accompaniment; epic may also mix several genres within its metrical narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of actions, characters, and affects via rhythm/voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain manners, affects, and actions are imitated through rhythmic figures and the voice (perfiguratos numeros ... imitantur et mores, et affectus, et actiones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match meter and vocal texture to the character or emotion you wish to represent: choose rhythmic patterns and diction to embody manners and feelings (e.g., agitated rhythms for agitation, measured meters for dignity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice of medium for the object imitated
rubrics_metrics.description: Different arts imitate by different means: painters and sculptors use colors and figures; phonosci (mimic singers) by natural voice; poets and musical arts by number, speech, and harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the expressive medium that best renders your chosen object: visual elements for visual resemblance, vocal/music/metre/diction for dramatic or lyrical imitation; do not force a medium unsuited to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and method: begin from first principles
rubrics_metrics.description: In exposition, proceed according to the nature of the things to be said, beginning from the first (initio secundum rerum dicendarum naturam ducto, primum a primis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure your composition so foundational elements and primary principles appear first; develop complexity only after establishing the basic parts and their relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible mixing of genres (especially in epic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Epic may permit the mixing of several of those kinds within itself (aut plura eorum genera permiscuerit inter se, quod aliae imitationes non faciant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider genre-mixing when appropriate—epics may incorporate lyrical, dramatic, or didactic elements—while ensuring the mixture serves unity and purpose rather than creating incoherence.
